name: unity
title: Unity
author: HydraOps
description: Unity's own MCP server (the Unity CLI with the Unity Pipeline package) for a Unity 6 editor open on this computer: build scenes, create and place objects, set components and materials, manage packages, capture the Scene and Game views, read the console, run tests and builds. Nine tools run or write code inside the editor; every call of those waits for your approval.

notes: Unity 6 (6000.x) with a project that has the Unity Pipeline package (com.unity.pipeline) installed, and the editor open on that project while the agent works. Without an open editor the connection has no tools; it picks them up by itself when the editor opens.

The Unity CLI: Unity Hub installs it; otherwise `winget install Unity.CLI` (Windows), `brew install --cask unity-cli` (macOS, Linux) or Unity's install script. It updates itself, so this connection cannot pin its version (classified with CLI 1.0.0-beta.12 and Pipeline 0.8.0-exp.1).

UNITY_PROJECT (Add-ons → MCP servers) is the folder of the project to drive. Empty, the server attaches to the editor that is open; with a folder, it finds that project's editor and the captures the tools save inside the project reach the chat.
HydraOps 0.1.63 or newer: earlier versions do not know the `unity` launcher, the UNITY_PROJECT placeholder or the tools that always ask.

setup.then: Prints the CLI's version. If the command is not found, install the Unity CLI (link below) and reopen HydraOps so it sees the new PATH.

tips: Give the whole connection to an agent with one line in its tools, `unity`. An agent that only builds scenes does not need the nine tools that run or write code (eval, eval_file, run_script, write_text_file, create_script, reload_file and its two variants, menu): list the tools it needs by name instead.
Open the project in the Unity editor before asking. If the editor was closed when HydraOps started, the connection shows no tools until it is open; it picks them up by itself within a minute.

To see the scene, ask for a capture: capture_scene_view and capture_game_view hand the picture to an agent whose model sees images. With UNITY_PROJECT set, a capture saved inside the project (save_path, or the screenshot tool) also appears under the reply.

Importing an asset package or adding a UPM package is one approval, not one per object: package_add downloads code from the internet and waits for you; the objects the agent then creates from it do not, unless the task has read outside content.
